household: Mama, Papa, Ella, Henny, Sarah, Charlotte and Gertie, later baby Charlie
creator: Sydney Taylor
address_as_given: the crowded tenement house section of the lower East Side
notes: The novels never give a street. The first book describes a four-room apartment taking up a whole floor of a two-story private house, and puts Papa's junk shop in a warehouse basement "not far from the river." Rivington Street is only where Mama shops, at the market. The family stays here through All-of-a-Kind Family Downtown and most of More All-of-a-Kind Family. The real Brenner family, on whom the books are based, lived at 708 East 5th Street near Avenue C when the author's sister Sarah was born in 1904, according to Hadassah Magazine. The mark is the neighborhood, not that address.
source_quote: Ella, Henny, Sarah, Charlotte, and Gertrude are five sisters growing up on the Lower East Side of Manhattan in 1912.
source2_quote: There’s the move from the Lower East Side up to the Bronx, which ends the book.

household: Mama, Papa, Ella, Henny, Sarah, Charlotte and Gertie, later baby Charlie
creator: Sydney Taylor
notes: The family moves at the end of More All-of-a-Kind Family ("It's just a subway ride to the Bronx," Mama says), and Uptown is set there in 1917. The books name the borough and nothing smaller, so this mark only says "somewhere in the Bronx." It sits in the south-central Bronx near Morris High School, which the author attended after her real family made the same move.
source_quote: It’s 1917. The family has moved to the Bronx.
source2_quote: There’s the move from the Lower East Side up to the Bronx, which ends the book.
